data.title: Keratolysis exfoliativa — viva
data.body:
_Viva questions for the case: **Keratolysis exfoliativa** (Eczemas)_

**Q1. What is keratolysis exfoliativa?**
- Lamellar dyshidrosis — recurrent focal superficial peeling of palms (and soles) beginning as air-filled 'blisters' that rupture into collarettes of scale, without inflammation

**Q2. Associations?**
- Summer, hyperhidrosis, friction, detergents; atopy; may be a variant of dyshidrotic eczema; possible keratin/corneodesmosin defects

**Q3. Differential diagnosis?**
- Pompholyx, tinea manuum (KOH), irritant hand dermatitis, acral peeling skin syndrome (TGM5), pitted keratolysis (soles), psoriasis, secondary syphilis

**Q4. Treatment?**
- Reassurance (self-limiting), avoid irritants, emollients, urea/lactic acid creams, barrier creams; treat hyperhidrosis

## Quick spotter facts
- Collarettes of peeling on palms without inflammation — keratolysis exfoliativa

_Sources: DYP Survival Guide for PG Dermatology Exam (Keratolysis exfoliativa); IADVL Textbook of Dermatology 5e ch.24. Answers written in our own words; check with your teachers' preferences._
